A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Soft-Rank Diffusion work. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST sorting and TSP experiments in Tables 1–2 and component ablations in Table 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original CIFAR-10 jigsaw results, reference-distribution tests, spatial error analyses, and inference timings.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds a KV-cached inference option for cGPL and Pointer-cGPL, reusing attention keys and values across prefix positions; Table 9 compares cached and uncached decoding. The reflected bridge, denoiser architectures, training objective, and core sampling algorithms are otherwise retained.

E1.justification: v2 adds CIFAR-10 jigsaw reconstruction at 3×3, 4×4, and 8×8 grids. This introduces natural-image spatial reconstruction beyond the retained numerical sorting and routing tasks, substantially broadening evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The learned comparator sets in MNIST and TSP remain unchanged, and jigsaw reuses SymmetricDiffusers. The new spatial error analyses additionally compare against an explicit random-assignment reference in Figures 4 and 7. The alternative relaxation spaces in Table 7 are discussed without experimental evaluation.

E3.justification: v2 adds matched and mismatched training/evaluation reference-distribution protocols at 4×4 with noise scale 0.5 and T=5, per-position and Manhattan-displacement diagnostics, and cached/uncached timing on 10,000 samples using one H100. The new jigsaw comparison matches seven-layer backbones. Original MNIST and TSP splits, budgets, and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the unchanged MNIST component ablation, v2 tests sensitivity to uniform versus Gaussian references and train/evaluation mismatch in Appendix C.1. Figures 4 and 7 analyze positional errors, while Figure 6 and Table 9 examine caching benefits and accuracy/runtime tradeoffs. These add substantial robustness and failure-analysis evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's description of differences as 'within noise' supplies no uncertainty estimate; Figure 6's shading represents cache speedup, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original MNIST, TSP, and component-ablation values are unchanged. New Table 3 reports 8×8 jigsaw exact-match accuracies of 0.0000 for SymmetricDiffusers, 0.0924 for cGPL, and 0.2700 for Pointer-cGPL. Tables 5–6 and 9 and Figures 4, 6, and 7 add reference-sensitivity, timing, and spatial-error results, substantially expanding the reported evidence.

T1.justification: Appendix B's reverse Gaussian-bridge derivation is unchanged. New Appendix C adds supplementary mathematical content, especially the chamber definition in Eq. 29 and assertions about equal volumes, the induced uniform prior, and margins. Its claim that LiftToGrid produces the chamber centroid conflicts with the endpoint-inclusive grid in Eq. 2.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims about soft-rank diffusion, hybrid reverse sampling, contextualized denoisers, and long-sequence advantages. The introduction adds jigsaw as supporting evaluation without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 introduces explanations involving autoregressive error accumulation, local versus global corruption, and the accuracy/runtime tradeoff. Appendix C adds interpretations of reference insensitivity, representation costs, and chamber-based robustness, and identifies constrained-permutation experiments as future work. These substantially extend the scientific interpretation beyond v1.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents KV caching and teacher-forced parallel training, identifies the uniform reference used in the main experiments, and supplies settings for reference tests and timing measurements. Existing Appendix A implementation details remain unchanged. Detailed jigsaw training and preprocessing instructions are still sparse.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for CIFAR-10, KV caching, Sinkhorn projection, and Hungarian assignment: Krizhevsky, Pope et al., Sinkhorn, and Kuhn. Appendix C.2 also positions rank-vector relaxation against Birkhoff and orthogonal representations. The main related-work discussion and original positioning are largely retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are preserved. Local expansions add the caching discussion, Section 4.3, and an analysis appendix, moving the former Appendix C to D. Other edits include standardizing much of n to N, changing bibliography style, and updating the publication and correspondence text.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with positional heatmaps, displacement distributions, an accuracy/runtime plot, and new benchmark, robustness, representation-comparison, and timing tables. Existing displays are retained with relocation or renumbering, including architecture Figure 4 becoming Figure 5 and ablation Table 4 becoming Table 8.

improvement.justification: The new spatial-task evaluation, reference robustness tests, and measured inference costs improve empirical support and make the accuracy/runtime tradeoff assessable. The benefit is tempered by sparse jigsaw training documentation and the new centroid claim in Appendix C.3, which conflicts with Eq. 2's grid containing 0 and 1. The original results and reverse-kernel derivation remain intact, supporting a limited net improvement.
